newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen press calls for tax on IPO subscribers.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen press calls for tax on IPO subscribers.

text.p: An official Shenzhen-based newspaper on Friday urged securities authorities to levy a tax on subscribers of initial public offerings to reduce speculation in China's primary A share market.
"The tax would increase IPO subscription costs," the Securities Times said in a commentary.
"Only it (a tax) can effectively rein in excessive speculative activities in IPO subscriptions," it said.
The newspaper suggested a 0.3 percent tax on funds deposited for share subscriptions, which have attracted enormous amounts of money since Beijing relaunched its stock market expansion in early 1996.
Nearly every A share issue, denominated in Chinese yuan and restricted to mainland Chinese, has been heavily over-subscribed and skyrocketed on debut.
